candidate.answerReason: The unit grid gives an enclosing right triangle of area 6. Removing two triangles of areas 4 and 3/2 leaves area 1/2.

methods.label: Subtract from a larger right triangle
methods.explanation:
The narrow triangle has no horizontal or vertical side, so enclose it in a right triangle whose base and height can be counted on the grid. Let \(D\) be the bottom-right grid point, directly below \(C\) and on the same horizontal row as \(A\). Counting unit gaps gives \(AD=4\) and \(CD=3\), so
\[
\text{area of }ACD=\frac{4\times3}{2}=6.
\]
Draw \(BD\). The three triangles \(ABD\), \(BCD\), and \(ABC\) fill triangle \(ACD\) without overlapping interiors. Point \(B\) is \(2\) units above \(AD\), so triangle \(ABD\) has area \(4\times2\div2=4\). Point \(B\) is \(1\) unit horizontally from \(CD\), so triangle \(BCD\) has area \(3\times1\div2=\frac32\). Subtracting these two pieces gives
\[
\text{area of }ABC
=6-4-\frac32
=\boxed{\frac12}
\]
square unit, choice B.
